description_full: Niterra Co., Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and sells spark plugs and related products in Japan and internationally. The company offers automotive parts, such as spark plug, spark plug cable, power cable, ignition coil, O2 sensor, knock sensor, and radiator cap; semiconductor packages, such as ceramic package, substrate for probe card, package for optical communications, and high-frequency rf ceramic packages; semiconductor manufacturing equipment products, including electrostatic chuck, vacuum chuck, thermal spraying, regeneration products; medical equipment, such as oxygen concentrators and liquid oxygen systems; industrial ceramic parts, including balls for bearings, piezoelectric ceramics, and other industrial ceramics; and other products. The company was formerly known as NGK Spark Plug Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Niterra Co., Ltd. in April 2023. Niterra Co., Ltd. was founded in 1936 and is headquartered in Nagoya, Japan.

financial_summary: NITERRA CO LTD. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $20.1B market cap on $4.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 7% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $612M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 28× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
